summary: Constructs the actual geometric curve zero-potential reference measure, with independent real Cartier comparison, model independence, residue/gauge weights, and locality and continuity at zero arity.
detailedSummary: For every excellent reduced local curve, proves mu_a=sum_q f_q ord_q(a) delta_(ord_q/ord_q(a)). A finite normalization graph and local snake-sequence length argument identify this with independent Cartier zero-cycle degree on every actual primary model. Treats full branch fibres, mixed-zero bounded profiles, smooth DVR and empty cases. A normalization of generic degree one and residue degree d demonstrates why residue weights are necessary. This is not a positive-arity higher-dimensional theorem.
text:
Let R be an excellent reduced local curve, with finite normalization having DVR centres S_q. Put f_q=[kappa(q):kappa(m)] and a_q=ord_q(a)>0. Every centred semivaluation of a DVR is a positive multiple of its order: a nonzero element is a uniformizer power times a unit, and units have value zero. Its support cannot be the maximal ideal, because the boundary ideal would then have infinite value. G331's normalization presentation therefore identifies the ENTIRE boundary with the finite discrete branch set v_q=ord_q/a_q. A regular conductor element has finite order on every branch, so all fibres here are singletons. Branches mean local normalization centres, not merely minimal components.

Define geometrically, before ideal-moment comparison,
mu_(a,R)=sum_q f_q a_q delta_(v_q). (5)
These are actual residue-degree weights, with no vertical generic degree.

We prove independent Cartier comparison on any actual primary model Y=Bl_I R. The ideal IS is invertible on the semilocal normal curve, so the blowup universal property gives h:Spec S→Y. This morphism is finite: its graph is closed in Spec S×_R Y because Y is separated, and projection to Y is finite as a base change of normalization. Its finite closed image contains every generic component point of the reduced primary blowup, hence is all of Y. Locally it is the finite normal birational extension with the same total quotient fields, so it is normalization. This proves domination of the stated primary curve models directly; no higher-dimensional arbitrary-model cofinality is assumed.

For an effective integral exceptional Cartier divisor A on Y, define its independent Cartier zero-cycle degree by
Degree_R[A]=sum_y length_(O_(Y,y))(O_(Y,y)/(g_y)) [kappa(y):kappa(m)],
using regular local equations g_y. Its support is finite: the finite normalization surjects onto Y and has finite closed fibre. These local rings are reduced one-dimensional rings, and the quotients have finite length. Residue fields are finite over the base residue field. This is the ordinary actual Cartier zero-cycle, not a degree defined by moments.

For the normalization comparison put T=O_(Y,y), let N be its finite semilocal normalization, and C=N/T. The module C has finite length because normalization is generically identical on a reduced curve. Multiplication by the regular local equation g in 0→T→N→C→0 yields
0→C[g]→T/gT→N/gN→C/gC→0.
The multiplication sequence for finite-length C gives length(C[g])=length(C/gC), so length_T(T/gT)=length_T(N/gN). Its DVR factors give
length_T(N/gN)=sum_(q→y) [kappa(q):kappa(y)] ord_q(g).
Multiply by [kappa(y):kappa(m)] and sum. Thus
Degree_R[A]=sum_q f_q ord_q(h^*A). (6)
No normality or Cohen–Macaulay assumption on Y was used.

G331's actual Cartier order-unit assertion writes any integral exceptional Cartier divisor F as a difference of effective exceptional Cartier divisors. Extend (6) by differences and finite real linear combinations. Local orders are homomorphisms on actual Cartier divisors, so relations cause no ambiguity. G331's evaluation at a branch is f_F(v_q)=ord_q(h^*F)/a_q. Hence
Integral f_F dmu_(a,R)=Degree_R(F). (7)
Both sides are unchanged under any common primary-model pullback because the pullback to normalization is unchanged. This proves actual model independence and independent real Cartier intersection comparison in dimension one.

For a primary ideal J, one-variable multiplicity additivity on the finite generically rank-one normalization, or n4's degree-one coefficient formula, gives
 e_R(J)=sum_q f_q ord_q(J)=Integral v(J) dmu_(a,R).
Indeed each DVR has primary Hilbert function with leading coefficient ord_q(J). Thus the independently geometric measure (5) agrees with n3's zero-potential moment measure; it was not defined by assigning moments and renaming them intersections.

The bounded geometric class on this finite branch set is every finite nonpositive vector. Each DVR cone is all nonpositive constants, obtained from parameter powers with real coefficients; the semilocal class is their finite product. Singleton normalization fibres and G331's positivity descent give every such vector downstairs. The actual decreasing completion is every extended nonpositive vector; bounded vectors are already continuous. All-zero and mixed-zero profiles are allowed as boundary functions, without a literal radial-extension identification.

There are zero potential entries. Therefore any two zero-tuples give the same measure on every open region, proving actual locality at this zero arity; every bounded descending-net statement for the zero-tuple is constant equality. This is not advertised as a positive-arity Bedford–Taylor theorem. Continuous tests have the usual finite-set continuity.

For another primary gauge b, put b_q=ord_q(b). The section map sends v_q to ord_q/b_q and multiplies its mass by b_q/a_q, exactly equation (3). Normalization is equation (4) with weights f_q. A smooth DVR over its own residue field has mass a_q at ord/a_q; maximal-ideal reference mass is one. Dimension zero has empty boundary and the zero measure without negative arity.

Here is an actual nontrivial residue-degree example. For any finite field extension k⊂l of degree d>1, possibly inseparable, let R=k+t l[[t]]⊂S=l[[t]]. With A=k[[t]] and a k-basis 1,alpha_2,...,alpha_d of l, R=A⊕sum_(i≥2) tA alpha_i. It is a finite A-algebra, hence Noetherian and excellent. It is local with maximal ideal tS and residue field k: elements with nonzero constant in k have inverses with constant in k. Its fraction field is l((t)), since t alpha/t=alpha. Thus S is finite normalization with GENERIC degree one but RESIDUE degree d. The conductor is tS; a conductor unit would force l=k.

For a=tS, formula (5) is d delta_(ord_t). For J=t^rS, J^N=t^(rN)S. A k-basis of R/J^N consists of 1 and alpha_j t^i for 1≤i<rN and 1≤j≤d. Hence length_R(R/J^N)=1+d(rN−1) and e_R(J)=dr. This is the correct moment and Cartier degree. Replacing the residue weight by generic degree one would incorrectly give r.
